$comment: The single source of truth for which MCP servers this toolkit ships and how
each one is installed, configured and probed. setup.sh, setup.ps1,
scripts/install_vendored.py, scripts/write_mcp_config.py and
scripts/verify_toolkit.py all read this file -- add a server here and every
one of them picks it up. Nothing else hardcodes the list.
Every server now lives under servers/ and is tracked in git. `origin` says
where the code came from, which is what decides who fixes its bugs and how
an update is pulled in:
first-party  written or forked here; we own it and fix it
vendored     copied verbatim from upstream; update via docs/licensing.md
`runtime` says how the server is reached:
stdio        launched as a subprocess by the MCP client
in-app       a plugin running inside the application, reached over HTTP
Vendoring GPL-3.0 code (Blockbench) is why this project is GPL-3.0 rather
than permissive. See docs/licensing.md and COPYRIGHT.
Placeholders in client entries, resolved by scripts/write_mcp_config.py:
{path}              absolute path to the server's `path` above
{venvScript:NAME}   the console script NAME inside that server's .venv
{app:KEY}           absolute path to a detected application
{port}              bridge.port, after probing bridge.portCandidates
name: gamedev-toolkit-mcp

obsidian.owns: Design docs, task lists, notes -- planning before building

install.$comment: The server's own package cannot be the import check -- importing mcp_obsidian raises unless OBSIDIAN_API_KEY is set. mcp.server is what it actually depends on (`from mcp.server import Server`) and has no import-time side effects.

obsidian.appSetup: Install the "Local REST API" community plugin in Obsidian, then run scripts/configure_obsidian.py to copy its key into mcp_config.json.

fallbackClient.$comment: Used when uv is not on PATH. cwd is what makes -m resolvable.

aseprite.appSetup: None -- the server spawns `aseprite --batch` per call.

blockbench.owns: 3D models, UV maps, model textures, bone rigs

install.$comment: The source is vendored here for licence compliance and reference, but the plugin runs inside Blockbench and is loaded by the app, not built by this repo.
steps: Blockbench > File > Plugins > Load Plugin from URL
Grant the network permission it asks for
Leave Blockbench open -- the plugin serves the MCP endpoint from inside the app

blockbench.appSetup: Blockbench must be open with the plugin loaded before any tool answers.

bridge.$comment: The plugin does not always land on 3000. write_mcp_config.py probes the candidates and pins whichever answers; check the plugin's status bar if none do.

install.$comment: The <2 pin matters. This server imports mcp.server.fastmcp, which mcp 2.0 removed, and its own dependency is unpinned -- a fresh install picks 2.x and dies at startup with ModuleNotFoundError. verifyImport targets that exact module: any later `uv pip install` into this venv can re-resolve mcp to 2.x and silently break it again.

client.$comment: The entry point is the console script `audacity-mcp`. `python -m audacity_mcp` does not work -- the package has no __main__.py.

audacity.appSetup: Audacity 3.x only (4.x is unsupported upstream). Enable Edit > Preferences > Modules > mod-script-pipe, then restart Audacity.

godot-mcp.appSetup: Copy servers/godot/addons/godot_mcp/ into your Godot 4 project and enable it under Project > Project Settings > Plugins, or run scripts/install_godot_plugin.py. The headless tools need none of this.
